title: A Thousand Won of Comfort
description:
The last train is gone. A coin noraebang in a back alley.
A thousand won for four songs. Inside the booth, it's just me.

A sticky vinyl couch, one tambourine, and the number for a ballad I know by heart.
Today weighed a lot.

choices.text: Sing my lungs out — let the next booth hear it
choices.result_text:
Punched in two more songs. The screen flashed 88 points, and a burst of canned applause played to an empty room.

I think I finally understand why so many people cry in noraebang booths.
The week felt a little lighter.

choices.text: Hit record — to listen to later
choices.result_text:
Saved the file. I'll cringe when I play it back at home.

But I wanted to leave today's version of me somewhere.
A thousand-won time capsule.

Just one. I didn't have the energy for more.
Still, I walked out of the alley lighter than I walked in.

title: PC Bang Ramyeon
description:
A rainy afternoon. Nowhere to go, so I ducked into a PC bang.
Fifteen hundred won an hour. The part-timer assigns me a seat number.

The smell of someone's instant ramyeon drifts over the monitor from the next seat.
— Why does PC bang ramyeon taste better?

choices.text: Order ramyeon, play a round — take it easy today
choices.result_text:
Ramyeon with an egg cracked in, and one round of a game. One round became three.

Half guilt, half bliss.
Still, on a rainy day there's no better hideout than a PC bang.

choices.text: Skip the game, just look things up
choices.result_text:
Used the high-res monitor to dig through job postings and property prices.
Faster internet than home — worth the fifteen hundred won.

choices.text: Just breathe in the smell and leave
choices.result_text:
In the end I didn't go in. I had to save even fifteen hundred won.
Walked off into the rain with only the smell of ramyeon to keep.

title: The Claw Machine Trap
description:
A claw machine corner by the subway exit.
Popular character plushies piled behind the glass. A thousand won a try.

"Two tries and I've got it, surely."
The moment that thought hits — it's already a trap.

choices.result_text:
The claw grabbed the plushie's head, then dropped it right before the chute.

"That thing's rigged." I knew it, and it still stung.
Still, walking away after only a thousand won — that's a win.

choices.text: Until it drops — my pride kicked in
choices.result_text:
Spent almost ten thousand won. The plushie finally came out.

Except now it's a ten-thousand-won plushie, not a thousand-won one.
Pride is always expensive. Can't chase Gangnam like this.

choices.text: Just take a photo and move on
choices.result_text:
Snapped a shot of my reflection in the glass with the plushies behind it.
Didn't buy the plushie, but I got a post out of it. That's the real win.

title: Seoul, Seen From Namsan
description:
Splurged and went up Namsan. Took the stairs instead of the cable car.
The observation-deck railing is crammed with lovers' padlocks.

Seoul spreads out endlessly below.
Somewhere in all those lights — is Gangnam.

choices.text: Hang a padlock — with a wish written on it
choices.result_text:
'Gangnam within five years. Kim Minjun.'
I wrote it knowing how corny it was.

The 'click' of the lock closing felt strangely solid.
Every one of those other padlock owners had their own Gangnam too, I bet.

choices.text: Just look at the city for a long while
choices.result_text:
It hit me that not one of those countless lights was my room.

And yet — that someday one of those Gangnam lights would be mine,
tonight I decided to just believe it. Believing is free.

title: Ramyeon and Chimaek by the Han River
description:
The weather broke. I grabbed a picnic mat and headed to the Han River.
There's a long line at the convenience-store instant-ramyeon machine.

The mat next to mine has delivery chicken spread out.
The river glitters. The cheapest luxury in Seoul.

choices.text: Delivery chicken and beer — just for today
choices.result_text:
A whole fried chicken on the mat, a can of beer.
Han River chimaek. Nothing special, and somehow everything.

One piece of chicken and five years slipped my mind for a moment.
I started wondering how I'd ever explain this to a foreign friend, and laughed.

choices.text: Convenience-store ramyeon and a canned beer — best value
choices.result_text:
Four thousand won of happiness from the ramyeon machine.
The river breeze blew across the broth.

It'd be a lie to say I didn't envy the chicken mat next door —
but tonight the Han River was fair to everyone.

choices.text: Just watch the river and head home
choices.result_text:
Sat for an hour without buying a thing.
The river was free.

The most expensive comfort was, today, the cheapest.
